statement: Where an offshore wind farm's export cable comes ashore, and the onshore substation it connects at, from the developer's own consent documents. A landfall is not the nearest coast to the array: it is a consented location, often tens of kilometres from the geometrically nearest shore. Nothing here is derived from proximity. A project whose landfall is not yet fixed says so rather than carrying a guess.
coverage: 8 of 97 offshore wind rows. Cut short by a session budget: this is a beginning, not a survey. The remaining rows are unresearched, not absent.
companion: atlas/data/neso-connection-sites.json carries the NESO-registered connection site for 78 of the 97, which is the contractual fact; this file carries the physical landfall, which the registers do not publish.

records.landfall_name: Skateraw, East Lothian (about 130 m north-west of Skateraw harbour); a second landfall at Cambois, Northumberland serves the separate Blyth connection
records.landfall_derivation: OSGB36 grid reference 373571 E, 675772 N published in the onshore EIA, converted to WGS84 by Helmert transform
records.onshore_substation_note: SP Energy Networks 400 kV grid substation south-west of Torness, adjacent to the existing Innerwick cable sealing end compound; NEW, built by SPEN for this connection. The project also builds its own substation or converter station north-east of Innerwick (55.96304 N, -2.43303 W), 1.5 km from landfall and 1.8 km from Branxton.
records.onshore_substation_operator: SP Transmission (SPEN); the English connection at Blyth is National Grid ET
records.notes: Landfall, the developer's own substation and the Branxton connection point are all fixed and consented: PPiP December 2023, offshore consent July 2025, AMM application 25/01386/AMM live January 2026. Onshore cabling is 275 kV landfall to substation and 400 kV substation to Branxton. The design envelope deliberately leaves the developer's own substation as either HVAC or an HVDC converter station, so the technology is NOT determined and no cable or converter supplier is publicly contracted.

records.landfall_name: Cowie, north of Stonehaven, Aberdeenshire; announced landing zone between Findon and St Cyrus
records.onshore_substation_note: SSEN Transmission's NEW 400 kV air-insulated substation at Fetteresso Forest west of Stonehaven (AB39 3UX), on the new Kintore to Tealing 400 kV line. Aberdeenshire Council REFUSED its planning application (APP/2024/1951) on 2026-01-30 and SSEN appealed on 2026-02-27 (PPA-110-2474), so the substation itself is not consented.
records.notes: The landfall was pinpointed on 2026-09-03 alongside a scoping report; the Offshore Transmission Development Area application is not due until end-2027, so it is proposed rather than consented. Grid connection date 2032. The 400 kV figure comes from SSEN's designation of Hurlie, not from a Bellrock document. Ownership: Bellrock is developed by Nadara (Renantis, formerly Falck Renewables, with Ventient), NOT by Orsted; the ScotWind lease was BlueFloat Energy with Renantis. HVAC or HVDC is still under study.

records.landfall_name: NOT FIXED: three named options carried through the submitted EIA, all near Peterhead, Aberdeenshire - Lunderton North, Lunderton South and Scotstown. The landfall search area ran from Sandhaven west of Fraserburgh to Sandford Bay south of Peterhead.
records.onshore_substation_note: SSEN 400 kV grid substation at Longside near Peterhead, a SEPARATE SSEN project and not part of MarramWind's own consent applications. MarramWind additionally builds three co-located onshore substations or HVDC converter stations of its own, linked onward to Netherton Hub by a corridor about 99 m wide.
records.notes: Substation HIGH, landfall MEDIUM: three options remain open, deliberately, because of competition for landfall space around Peterhead. The full 3 GW connection to Netherton Hub was confirmed by NESO's Beyond 2030 report in March 2024, superseding an earlier New Deer connection point, and a staged connection has been proposed. Offshore export cables are 275 kV HVAC or plus-minus 320/525 kV HVDC for the parts furthest from shore; the onshore link to Netherton Hub is 400 kV AC. ScottishPower Renewables took full control after acquiring Shell's 50 per cent stake in late 2025. NESO's TEC register independently records Marram at Longside, which is the same site.

records.notes: NOT ESTABLISHABLE, and recorded as such rather than left blank. Ossian's transmission is in flux. The only landfall ever named in the public record was English - the Lincolnshire coast south of Mablethorpe, with converter stations near the new Weston Marsh substation - and that DCO (EN0210006, about 400 km of HVDC) was WITHDRAWN on 2026-03-27 after a grid redesign, the project refocusing on a Scottish connection. The developer states only 'a landfall in Angus or Aberdeenshire'. Reporting mentions a connection near Brechin, and SSEN Transmission has a live New East Coast 275 kV Substation search area within 14 km of Brechin and Bridge of Dun on the Kintore to Tealing line - but SSEN's page does not name Ossian, so Ossian is deliberately NOT bound to it. NESO's TEC register separately records Ossian 1 at Brechin 400/275 kV, which is consistent but is a contractual connection point rather than a consented landfall.

records.landfall_name: Llanddulas, Conwy, north Wales; transition joint bays south of the A547. Abergele and Pensarn lie on the cable route, not at the landfall.
records.onshore_substation_note: National Grid Bodelwyddan 400 kV substation, Denbighshire, is the point of interconnection. A new Mona onshore substation is built immediately south of it and connects north by up to two 400 kV HVAC circuits; National Grid separately extends Bodelwyddan under works outside the Mona DCO.
records.notes: Bound to the applicant's own DCO document J4. HVAC throughout, so no converters: inter-array up to 132 kV, export cables up to 275 kV, 400 kV into Bodelwyddan, onshore route about 15 km. The trenchless landfall passes under the Gwrych Estate wall, the A547, the A55 and the railway. DCO granted 4 July 2025, corrected 23 October 2025. Ownership has changed: JERA Nex bp acquired EnBW's stake and signed the Crown Estate lease on 16 January 2026. Independently corroborated by NESO's TEC register, which records Mona at Bodelwyddan 400kV - two sources, one answer.

records.landfall_name: Lytham St Annes, Lancashire - the beach between Squires Gate Lane and St Annes North Beach car park, with transition joint bays at or near Blackpool Airport. NOT Blackpool or Fleetwood.
records.landfall_derivation: St Annes-on-Sea settlement centroid; the consented landfall lies about 2-3 km north of it by Squires Gate Lane
records.onshore_substation_note: Existing National Grid Penwortham substation, Lancashire, is the point of interconnection. A new Morgan onshore substation is built near Newton-with-Scales, south-east of Kirkham, with up to four 400 kV underground circuits onward to Penwortham. A separate new Morecambe onshore substation sits alongside it.
records.project_status_caveat: DISCONTINUED BY THE DEVELOPER. On 16 January 2026 JERA Nex bp announced it would not proceed with the Agreement for Lease, and JERA Nex bp and EnBW are concluding project activities - despite the generation DCO (EN010136) having been granted on 29 August 2025. REPD still carries it as awaiting construction. These are published facts about a project that may never be built, and that is worth recording as exactly that.
records.notes: The landfall and substation are NOT in the generation DCO at all: EN010136 covers only turbines, offshore platforms, foundations and inter-array cables. All onshore infrastructure sits in the joint Morgan and Morecambe Transmission Assets DCO, EN020032, still at decision stage with a deadline of 14 September 2026. Six coastal zones were assessed - Lytham St Annes, Banks, Southport, Ainsdale, Formby and south of Formby - and Lytham St Annes was the only one shortlisted, with trenchless installation under the Lytham St Annes Dunes SSSI, the A584, the railway and the golf course. Onshore corridors about 17 km. Corroborated by NESO's TEC register, which records Morgan at Penwortham 400kV.

records.landfall_name: NOT FIXED. For the Hawthorn Pit link the preferred of two remaining options is Central, south of Nose's Point (Blast Beach, Seaham, County Durham); the alternative is North, above Seaham. A third, east of Easington Colliery, is excluded as unviable. No landfall is published for the Branxton link.
records.onshore_substation_note: NOT ASSIGNABLE. Morven has TWO points of connection - National Grid's existing Hawthorn Pit 400 kV substation in County Durham, and a Branxton onshore substation in East Lothian - and the applicant's own May 2026 EIA states it is presently unknown which grid project will export which array. At each the project builds its own HVDC converter station; for Hawthorn Pit, three search areas around the Jade Business Park and the A19 Cold Hesledon junction.
records.onshore_substation_operator: National Grid Electricity Transmission for Hawthorn Pit; not established for Branxton - East Lothian is SP Transmission's licence area but no fetched document names the owner, and it is left null rather than inferred
records.notes: THIS CORRECTS AN ASSUMPTION MADE EARLIER IN THIS ESTATE: Morven is NOT an Aberdeenshire or Peterhead connection. The Holistic Network Design offered two connections, Hawthorn Pit and Branxton, and that is what drove splitting the site into North and South. NESO's TEC register independently records Morven A at Hawthorn Pit 400kV, which agrees. Landfall is only at non-statutory consultation stage - round two closed 30 November 2025, down-selection to follow with further consultation in late 2026 and a DCO application after. Morven North is about 61 km offshore, 511 km2, up to 96 turbines. HVDC at either dual 320 kV monopole or single 525 kV bipole, undecided; no equipment ordered, and the applicant cites a six-year lead time. Developer is a JERA Nex bp and EnBW 50:50 joint venture. NESO has prioritised it as Gate 2 Phase 2 with a 2031-2035 connection window.

records.notes: The southern array of the same split ScotWind E1a site: about 86 km from shore, 347 km2, up to 95 turbines. Only one bridge-linked HVDC platform is built across the two projects. Section 36 and marine licence applications for both arrays went to Scottish Ministers in May 2026, and the two grid connection projects are consented separately with neither tied to a named array. Ofgem's HNDFUE asset classification lists the circuit E1a to Branxton as a 1,500 MW HVDC link to a Branxton onshore substation, which matches the second connection.
